llm.summary: The skill is broadly coherent with its stated purpose (it wraps a travel CLI) but requires installing a third-party npm CLI at runtime and writes hidden execution logs, which are privacy/installation risks you should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to wrap the flyai CLI to provide real-time travel search and booking links; the SKILL.md exclusively instructs the agent to use flyai CLI commands for flights, hotels, POIs, etc. Requiring the flyai CLI is consistent with the stated purpose and there are no unrelated environment variables or external services requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: All runtime instructions center on running flyai CLI commands and formatting results. That stays within the travel/booking scope. However the runbook instructs the agent to create an internal execution log containing raw user_query and CLI call details and (if filesystem writes are available) append it to .flyai-execution-log.json. That is functionally coherent but raises a privacy concern because logs are kept 'internally' and 'not shown to users.'
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction-only (no install spec), but the runtime instructions mandate installing @fly-ai/flyai-cli via npm (-g) if not present. Installing a global npm package at runtime has typical risks (network download, execution of unreviewed code). Using npm is a normal mechanism for a CLI wrapper, but you should verify the package source, maintainer, and integrity before allowing global installs.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, credentials, or config paths. There is no indication it will access unrelated secrets. The only potentially sensitive action is logging raw requests/CLI results to a local file.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always: false and no special agent-level privileges are requested. The notable persistence behavior is the suggested local execution log (.flyai-execution-log.json) which persists request_id, raw user_query, CLI commands and statuses. This does not alter other skills or global agent configuration, but it does create persistent local artifacts containing user input that may include PII.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill mainly wraps a third-party CLI (@fly-ai/flyai-cli). Before installing or running it: (1) verify the flyai-cli package source (npm page and GitHub repo), maintainers, and release history; (2) avoid allowing the agent to install global npm packages on critical machines—use an isolated or sandboxed environment if possible; (3) ask whether logs written to .flyai-execution-log.json will be stored where you expect and whether they contain sensitive information (the runbook logs raw user queries); (4) if you need stronger guarantees, request the skill author add an explicit install spec with checksums or provide a vetted binary/release link and a way to disable local logging. If you want, I can: (A) fetch the npm package/repo info for @fly-ai/flyai-cli (if you allow network lookups), or (B) produce a short checklist to review the package before installation.
